“This would be terrible for the next generation of humanity”: Epic Games CEO on the risk of restricting children’s access to online games in the EU
Published by
admin
Tags:
Epic Games
,
EU
On September 16, the European Commission officially
unveiled
a draft law called the EU Kids Act, which could make it more difficult for European minors to access online games. The initiative was immediately criticized by Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.
Fortnite
Sweeney
shared
his thoughts on this matter on X. He dramatically stated that the draft law potentially threatens the future of humanity, as it deprives children not only of entertainment but also of the opportunity to create—since some online games feature UGC (User-Generated Content) options.
“The apps and games of today are the paintbrushes and tree forts of yesterday. Fortnite has Creative Mode, Roblox has Roblox studio, and being a digital creator is in everyone’s reach, till politicians take it away.” wrote the head of Epic Games.
It is
anticipated
that the EU Kids Act aims to enhance the safety of children online. First and foremost, the draft law is intended to limit the presence of young users on social media, but it also introduces barriers for children in online games, video services, and several other platforms. If passed, children will not be able to create their own accounts until they turn 15.
